  "content": "All three symptoms — 429-backoff deadlock, calendar/Dream-Engine duplicate writes, and orphaned Engram state-dir entries — trace to the same gap: Siri's blackboard (shared filesystem state) has no unified write-coordination/checkpoint layer, so independent writers (event-loop sessions, dream cycles, calendar skills) race and duplicate rather than serializing through a shared mutex or structured checkpoint. Memory 37bd6188 explicitly names this missing piece — Engram lacks CC's 'structured checkpoint' capability — while CC's actual fix (triple-gate: time + session-count + mutex via .consolidate-lock, f7d12119/ac40d532/53d5823e) shows what a minimal lock-plus-gate abstraction over the blackboard would look like. The minimal fix is therefore not per-symptom patching but adding a single mutex/checkpoint mediator that all blackboard writers must acquire before mutating shared state.";

{"content":"All three symptom lines — 429-backoff deadlock, calendar/Dream-Engine duplication, and Engram state-dir orphans — converge on one root: Siri's blackboard (shared filesystem state) has no unified write-coordination or structured-checkpoint layer, so independently-triggered writers (event-loop sessions, dream cycles, calendar skills) race, duplicate-write, or leave stale state rather than serializing through a shared mutex. Memory 37bd6188 explicitly flags this as the missing piece in Engram versus CC, and CC's actual triple-gate mutex (time-lock + session-count + .consolidate-lock file, seen in f7d12119/ac40d532/53d5823e) is the concrete pattern Siri's blackboard lacks. This same gap likely underlies the 'leaky pipeline' anti-pattern and dispatch-without-criteria issues in bd6736d4, and the fork-subagent caching bug in ffd06c12, since all involve concurrent writers mutating shared state without a coordinating lock.","tensions":["Composite architecture (supervisor+pipeline+blackboard) optimizes for flexible dispatch but sacrifices the concurrency guarantees a pure blackboard model requires","CC's Dream/autoDream mutex+gate system is held up as the reference fix, yet Siri's Engram was designed as complementary rather than a drop-in replacement, creating ambiguity about where the lock layer should live","Symptoms are treated as independent bug reports (calendar dupes, 429 deadlock, state-dir drift) when evidence suggests a single missing abstraction, risking redundant local patches instead of one structural fix"],"source_ids":["37bd6188-df4","f7d12119-a45","ac40d532-a8a","53d5823e-1c3","dd3aef6d-a0c","bd6736d4-9ec","180972c5-725","ffd06c12-e03"],"confidence":0.75,"importance":9,"tags":["architecture","blackboard-pattern","concurrency","root-cause","engram"]}
